prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1375; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment kept growing well beyond what this injury usually needs, with more visits and new services added month after month.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: Claim reported by the policyholder's household member after a sideswipe while changing lanes. The claimant reports a knee injury and is represented by counsel, so all contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Obtained the police report and contacted the other driver, who described the lane change and contact in the same way the claimant did. Two independent witnesses were also reached and their accounts are consistent.

Entry 3: Reviewed the photos submitted from the scene. The damage is mostly along the expected line of the described impact, and the claimant's vehicle shows no sign of earlier damage in the same areas.

Entry 4: Confirmed with the police and the witnesses that the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the collision. The driver is listed on the policy as a household member, so coverage applies under the policy terms.

Entry 5: Spoke with the claimant's attorney, who provided the initial medical summary. The reported knee injury fits the kind and force of the collision, and no prior injury to that body area is known from the records available so far.

Entry 6: Recorded the claimant's account by phone. The version given is the same as the one provided at first notice, including the sequence of the lane change and the point of impact.

Entry 7: Verified the policy effective date and reviewed the vehicle history. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the start of coverage.

Entry 8: Treatment has grown steadily since the first report, with more visits and new services added each month. That pattern is well beyond what this type of knee injury usually requires, so the file has been flagged for a medical review.

Entry 9: Sent the damage estimate, the medical review request and the statement summaries to the supervisor for a settlement authority decision. The attorney has been notified that the file is under review and that a response on the medical question is pending.
